description: Single source of truth for the kit's prerequisites (tools, MCP servers, session skills). Read by scripts/preflight.sh (phase 0); cited by README.md and skills/legacy-upgrade/SKILL.md. `level` is the migration-pipeline gate: required = phase-0 hard fail, recommended = documented degradation. `requiredBy` lists the skills that hard-require the entry at their own preconditions step; `token` is the string CI expects in each of those skills' compatibility frontmatter (tests/skills/check-frontmatter.py). `requiresSdk` (optional, on an `mcps` entry) is the minimum .NET SDK MAJOR that server's own launcher needs, which may be higher than the pipeline's floor: below it the server cannot start, so scripts/preflight.sh names the floor instead of reporting the setup fine. An entry without the field is unaffected — absent is not "floor 0". `launcher` (optional, on an `mcps` entry) is the executable that starts that server, spelled as .mcp.json invokes it and always a bare command name rather than a path: its absence from PATH proves the shipped launcher cannot have started the server, so preflight probes it with `command -v` and reports the miss — `requiresSdk` is then the remedy that explains what to install about it. An entry without the field gets no probe and behaves exactly as before. Both fields are read by preflight only — hooks/roseline-gate.sh reaches the same conclusion for itself with a hardcoded `command -v dnx`, since a PreToolUse hook cannot afford to parse this file on every C# Read; tests/roseline/test.sh pins that hardcoded name to the `launcher` declared here, so the necessary duplication cannot drift. Add or remove a prerequisite HERE, never in a hard-coded list. Values must not contain tab characters (tab is the internal field separator).

tools.name: python3
tools.hint: required by the kit's scripts (inventory, dashboard)

tools.name: jq
tools.hint: required by hooks/roseline-gate.sh — without it the gate exits silently and C# Reads stop being enforced

tools.test: command -v google-chrome || command -v chromium || test -x '/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome'
